system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery
G6: Azure

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'
T3: Claiming GCP/BigQuery or Azure experience
T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given
T5: Reusing the old cover letter's 'two years at Adria Retail' framing as current
T6: Attributing Debezium/CDC when portfolio and notes are omitted (CV does not mention it)

# OUTPUT 1: CV
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer | Data Platform
Rijeka, Croatia | lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example
PROFILE
Senior Data Engineer with 9 years of experience designing, building and operating production data platforms and
cloud data warehouses across payments, e-commerce and logistics. Experienced in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt,
Spark, Kafka and AWS, with a strong background in dimensional data modeling, data quality and large-scale batch
and streaming pipelines. Focused on reliable, well-tested systems, clear data contracts and reusable platform
capabilities. MSc in Computer Science; AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate.
EXPERIENCE
Senior Data Engineer - Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. (logistics marketplace), Rijeka | 03/2022 -
present
• Own ingestion and orchestration for the company data platform, operating approximately 140 Airflow DAGs
loading data from PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake.
• Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures to more than 420 dbt models with tests and documentation;
introduced incremental models and state:modified CI in GitHub Actions, reducing nightly warehouse builds
from 5h10 to 1h35.
• Designed JSON Schema data contracts and CI checks between product and data teams, reducing
broken-pipeline incidents from approximately 9 per month to 2 per month.
• Designed and built a Kafka event pipeline using Kafka Connect and Snowpipe Streaming for shipment tracking,
handling approximately 30 million events per day with under 2-minute p95 end-to-end latency; added
dead-letter and replay tooling.
• Replaced hourly full-table extracts from the orders database with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica
CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
• Optimized Snowflake warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and unused-table usage, reducing monthly spend from
approximately $38,000 to $24,000 in 2024.
• Participate in the data platform on-call rotation (one week in six); mentor two mid-level data engineers and run
weekly platform office hours.
Data Engineer - Kovalent Pay (payments startup), Zagreb | 09/2019 - 02/2022
• Built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile bank settlement files against internal ledgers, processing
approximately 1.2 TB of raw files from S3 daily; reduced finance team’s manual month-end reconciliation from
approximately three days to four hours.
• Designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse schema with more than 30 fact and dimension tables for finance and
risk teams.
• Established Great Expectations data quality checks on critical finance tables.
• Developed an internal Python library for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access, adopted by four teams.
Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer - Adria Retail Group, Split | 06/2017 - 08/2019
• Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL processes feeding an on-premises SQL Server warehouse.
• Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron, making data loads easier to debug and
change.
• Built Power BI reports for store operations across more than 40 stores.
SELECTED OPEN-SOURCE & COMMUNITY CONTRIBUTIONS
• Contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider for a SaaS CRM API, fixing a pagination bug and
adding tests (Python, pytest, 2023).
• Presented “Data contracts without the hype” at a regional data meetup (2024).
• Teach SQL for beginners at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year since 2021.
EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science (Data Science track) - Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries
CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate | May 2024
SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data engineering: Airflow, dbt, PySpark, Spark, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Great Expectations
Warehousing & databases: Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server
Cloud & infrastructure: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, MSK), Docker, Terraform (basic), GitHub
Actions
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)
LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. I bring nine years of
experience designing, building and operating production data platforms and cloud data
warehouses at scale, with hands-on experience in Python, SQL, dimensional data modelling,
Airflow, dbt, AWS, Snowflake and Redshift. Halden Pay’s focus on a shared platform and
reusable capabilities aligns closely with the work I have done throughout my career.
At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own ingestion and orchestration for a platform with approximately
140 Airflow DAGs, and migrated stored procedures into dbt models. Introducing incremental
models and CI checks reduced nightly warehouse builds from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35
minutes. I have also established data contracts between product and data teams, built
Kafka-based streaming and CDC pipelines, and take part in the platform on-call rotation. This
work has strengthened my approach to reliable production systems, data contracts, data quality
standards, performance optimization and taking ownership of production issues.
My experience also includes building PySpark jobs on AWS EMR at Kovalent Pay to reconcile
bank settlement files against internal ledgers, processing approximately 1.2 TB of raw files daily.
The work reduced month-end manual reconciliation from about three days to four hours. I also
designed a dimensional data model and Redshift warehouse schema for finance and risk teams
and introduced Great Expectations checks on critical finance tables. At Lukovac Freight Hub, I
also optimized Snowflake warehouse sizing, auto-suspend settings and unused-table usage,
reducing monthly spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 in 2024. Alongside this
platform work, I have contributed two merged pull requests to an open-source Airflow provider
and presented on data contracts at a regional data meetup.
I would welcome the opportunity to bring this experience to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team
and help build dependable, reusable platform capabilities for analysts, data scientists and
product teams. I would be glad to discuss how my background could contribute.
Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
